Playbook.title: The Allvisor SME Ops Playbook
Playbook.lead: 11 traps that quietly drain the cashflow of Malaysian clinics, shops and service businesses — and exactly what to fix first.
Playbook.meta: Written for owners, not for IT people. Roughly 12 minutes to read.
Playbook.whyTitle: Read this before you pay for any business software
Playbook.whyBody: Most software ads shout “buy now”. This one does the opposite. Below is the checklist we wish every clinic, shop, salon, workshop and tuition centre had before they spent money on the wrong tool. Work through it honestly. If three or more traps describe your business, you are losing more money to admin than to competitors.
Playbook.trap1T: Running a niche business on generic software
Playbook.trap1S: Your patients are labelled “customers”. Your classes are labelled “appointments”. Every new staff member has to be taught a translation layer before they can do the job.
Playbook.trap1F: One organisation should equal one niche. The menus, the words and the workflow must match how your floor already talks.
Playbook.trap1C: Do the maths: if training a new hire takes three extra days because of vocabulary alone, and you hire four people a year, that is nearly two working weeks paid for nothing.
Playbook.trap2S: Unpaid invoices live in Excel, in a notebook, and in your head. You discover the real number when rent is due.
Playbook.trap2F: One live figure for unpaid, visible on the dashboard every morning, with the oldest debts listed first.
Playbook.trap2C: Most small operators carry two to four weeks of revenue in invoices they have simply forgotten to chase.
Playbook.trap3T: Ignoring LHDN until the deadline panics you
Playbook.trap3S: TIN missing, inconsistent invoice numbers, customer details half filled in. MyInvois becomes a weekend fire drill.
Playbook.trap3F: Build the habits early: store TIN and SST correctly per branch, keep invoice numbering in one clean pattern, and review anything rejected weekly.
Playbook.trap3C: The cost is not the software. It is the two or three weekends you will spend cleaning historical records under time pressure.
Playbook.trap4T: Forcing bookings and retail into one screen
Playbook.trap4S: A salon or clinic sells products at the counter, but treatment history sits somewhere else entirely — or nowhere.
Playbook.trap4F: Hybrid businesses need booking and point of sale side by side, without cramming everything into one “sales” page.
Playbook.trap4C: Every product sale that never gets tied back to the customer record is a repeat visit you cannot follow up.
Playbook.trap5T: Stock that does not match the shelf
Playbook.trap5S: The system sells items it never tracked. Month-end stock count turns into an argument.
Playbook.trap5F: Every sale, return and adjustment should move stock automatically, and low stock should raise its hand before a customer asks.
Playbook.trap5C: Shrinkage nobody measures is shrinkage nobody stops. Count one high-value shelf today and compare it to your records.
Playbook.trap6S: Staff argue over partial payments. There are handwritten IOUs in the drawer.
Playbook.trap6F: Invoice status on every record — unpaid, partial, paid — with the payment method captured at the counter.
Playbook.trap6C: Partial payments are where small businesses lose money silently, because no single person is accountable for the remainder.
Playbook.trap7S: Clinic language shows up inside the gym branch of the same group, because they share one account.
Playbook.trap7F: Isolate each niche into its own organisation and link the branches that genuinely belong together.
Playbook.trap7C: When reports mix two kinds of business, the numbers stop being decisions and start being arguments.
Playbook.trap8T: Teaching the team a new language every time you switch tools
Playbook.trap8S: Training takes weeks because the buttons do not match the job the person was hired to do.
Playbook.trap8F: Pick software where the words already match the floor, so training is about the work rather than the interface.
Playbook.trap8C: Staff who do not trust the system keep a private notebook. That notebook is where your data goes to die.
Playbook.trap9S: Cash drawer, unpaid invoices and pending submissions all wait until “tomorrow”, and tomorrow never has time.
Playbook.trap9F: A five-minute daily close: money in, money still owed, anything rejected, drawer counted, done.
Playbook.trap9C: A discrepancy found the same evening is a conversation. The same discrepancy found next month is an accusation you cannot prove.
Playbook.trap10T: Paying for modules you will never open
Playbook.trap10S: Your tuition centre account has manufacturing features in the menu, and the flow you actually need is buried three clicks deep.
Playbook.trap10F: Menus should be gated by what your niche genuinely needs, so the daily path is the shortest path.
Playbook.trap10C: Every unused menu item is a place for a tired staff member to make a mistake at 6pm.
Playbook.trap11T: Committing before you have proof of fit
Playbook.trap11S: You sign a twelve-month contract on the strength of a demo, then discover the mismatch in month two.
Playbook.trap11F: Run real invoices through it first. Judge it on your own numbers, on your own floor, with your own staff.
Playbook.trap11C: The only honest test of business software is a normal Tuesday, not a sales presentation.
Playbook.midCtaTitle: Recognise three or more of these?
Playbook.midCtaBody: Then the problem is not your discipline — it is that the tool was never shaped for your kind of business. Open a dashboard that already speaks your floor and see the difference on real invoices.
Playbook.auditLead: Six questions. Answer them honestly today rather than in the week of the deadline.
Playbook.audit1: Your company TIN is saved against the business, not written on a sticky note.
Playbook.audit2: Invoice numbers follow one clear pattern with no gaps you cannot explain.
Playbook.audit3: Customer details are captured at the point of sale, not chased afterwards.
Playbook.audit4: You can list unpaid against paid invoices on one screen, right now, without exporting anything.
Playbook.audit5: Somebody specific owns rejected and pending submissions, and reviews them weekly.
Playbook.audit6: You could produce last month’s invoices for an auditor within an hour.
Playbook.auditVerdict: Any box you could not tick is not a software problem yet. It becomes one the week the deadline lands.
Playbook.nicheLead: Before you evaluate any system, write down the flows your business genuinely runs on. If a demo cannot show you all of them in ten minutes, it is not built for you.
Playbook.nicheCol2: Flows it must handle on day one
Playbook.nicheRow1B: Appointments, patient records, treatment invoices, follow-up recall
Playbook.nicheRow2B: Point of sale, stock movement, cash drawer close, supplier reorder
Playbook.nicheRow3B: Classes, attendance, term fees, parent communication
Playbook.nicheRow4B: Memberships, class schedule, check-ins, renewal reminders
Playbook.nicheRow5B: Job cards, vehicle history, parts consumption, quotation to invoice
Playbook.nicheRow6B: Tables or rooms, occupancy, shift close, daily takings
Playbook.endBody: Pick the single trap that costs you the most money this month and fix that one first. You do not need new software to start — you need to know which hole you are pouring cash into. When you want the dashboard that closes those holes for your specific niche, Allvisor takes a few minutes to set up and nothing to try.

StartLanding.whyBoxBody: Because shouting “buy our software” only speaks to the small handful of owners ready to buy today. Everybody else is still researching, still comparing, and still getting burned by systems that call patients “customers”. We would rather be useful to you now and earn the sale later. And frankly: if a free report already fixes something in your business, you can guess what the paid product is like.
StartLanding.problemTitle: The real problem is not that you need software
StartLanding.problemBody: It is that the wrong software forces your floor to speak a foreign language. Clinics inherit retail words. Gyms inherit tuition wording. Shops drown in appointment screens they will never open. Every mismatch costs training time, missed invoices, and unpaid balances you only find out about when rent is due.
StartLanding.problemBody2: And because the mismatch never shows up on demo day, most owners end up blaming themselves. They assume they are disorganised. They are not. They were handed a tool shaped for somebody else’s business.
StartLanding.agitateTitle: Leave it alone and the cost compounds
StartLanding.agitate1T: Staff quietly build a second system.
StartLanding.agitate1B: A private notebook, a WhatsApp group, a spreadsheet nobody else can read. Your real data walks out of the software and into somebody’s handbag.
StartLanding.agitate2B: They do not disappear. They just stop being visible until the month you cannot cover a bill.
StartLanding.agitate3B: TIN, invoice numbering and half-filled customer details all get cleaned up under deadline pressure instead of during normal work.
StartLanding.agitate4B: Nobody measures the gap, so nobody closes it, and month-end becomes an argument between people who are all telling the truth.
StartLanding.agitate5B: Not because you are needed there, but because you have no way of knowing what happened while you were out.
StartLanding.agitateClose: None of these ever appear as a line item in your accounts. That is exactly why they survive for years.

Admin.title: Admin
Admin.subtitle: Manage categories, services, staff, plans and branches.
Admin.superSubtitle: Monitor and manage every linked branch in expandable groups.
Admin.lockHint: Admin page is locked. Default password = clinic/business name (no spaces) + year the account was created.
Admin.categoriesHint: Create categories first. Description is optional.
Admin.servicesHint: Assign each service to a category, set price, and optional description.
Admin.servicesHintRetail: Optional catalog items for invoices (inventory stock is managed separately).
Admin.needCategoryFirst: Add at least one category before creating services.
Admin.staffPasswordHint: If this person already has an Allvisor account, leave the password empty and we will link it. If they do not have one yet, set a password of at least 6 characters and the account is created for them right away.
Admin.addMemberHint: Enter a registered Allvisor email to add them as staff / supervisor / manager / co-admin. One account can only join one shop. Owner cannot be kicked.
Admin.addMemberHintTuition: Enter a registered Allvisor email to add them as staff / supervisor / manager / co-admin. One account can only join one tuition centre. Owner cannot be kicked.
Admin.addBranchHint: Enter the exact Allvisor clinic name of another branch (register that clinic separately first). If you are admin of both, it links immediately and appears in the branch list below. Otherwise their admin must approve.
Admin.addBranchHintRetail: Enter the exact Allvisor shop name of another branch (register that shop separately first). If you are admin of both, it links immediately. Otherwise their admin must approve.
Admin.addBranchHintTuition: Enter the exact Allvisor tuition centre name of another branch (register that tuition separately first). If you are admin of both, it links immediately and appears in the branch list below. Otherwise their admin must approve.
Admin.businessSettingsHint: Clinic / shop identity used on invoices and LHDN.
Admin.businessSettingsHintTuition: Tuition centre identity used on invoices and LHDN.
Admin.logoHint: Upload a logo, zoom/pan to crop, then pick round or square. Live previews show both frames before you save.
Admin.logoDragHint: Choose an image, then drag to position and zoom to crop
Admin.invoiceFormatHint: Controls auto invoice numbers. Customize prefix, digits, and the full pattern.
Admin.scorecardHint: Compare income, unpaid invoices, appointments and no-shows across linked clinics.
Admin.scorecardHintRetail: Compare income, unpaid invoices, transactions and low stock across linked shops.
Admin.scorecardHintTuition: Compare income, unpaid invoices and activity across linked tuition centres.
Admin.activityHint: Tracks staff actions visible to admins and supervisors.
Admin.serviceChargeHint: Applied automatically on every invoice as service tax (shown in small text before total).
Admin.clinicHoursHint: Per-branch settings. Controls Dashboard and Appointments timetables for this clinic. Last hour shown = closing hour.
Admin.tuitionHoursHint: Per-branch settings. Controls Dashboard and Schedule timetables for this tuition. Last hour shown = closing hour.
Admin.shopSettingsHint: Per-branch service charge applied on invoices for this shop.
Admin.tuitionSettingsHint: Per-branch service charge applied on invoices for this tuition centre.
Admin.holidayNote: Malaysian public holidays are auto-highlighted on the timetable for nurses to check.
Admin.holidayNoteTuition: Malaysian public holidays are auto-highlighted on the timetable for staff to check.

Lhdn.title: LHDN e-Invoice
Lhdn.subtitle: Allvisor submits e-Invoices to MyInvois as your authorized intermediary. Each shop uses its own TIN.
Lhdn.subtitleTuition: Allvisor submits e-Invoices to MyInvois as your authorized intermediary. Each tuition centre uses its own TIN.
Lhdn.brnHelp: For IG (individual) TIN: enter your NRIC from MyInvois Taxpayer Profile (ID Number). For company TIN (C…): enter ROB/ROC.
Lhdn.linkedConfirm: I authorized {name} as my intermediary in the MyInvois portal (Representatives → Intermediaries).
Lhdn.howTitle: How this works for your shop
Lhdn.howTitleTuition: How this works for your tuition centre
Lhdn.howStep1: Enter your Tax Identification Number (TIN) below and save.
Lhdn.howStep2: Log in to MyInvois → Representatives → Intermediaries → add {name}.
Lhdn.howStep3: Tick the confirmation that you authorized {name}, then save.
Lhdn.howStep4: Submit invoices from Allvisor — they go to LHDN under your TIN.
Lhdn.howNote: {name} holds one platform API credential. Your Client Secret is never required.
Lhdn.lockedPlan: Your plan does not include e-Invoice. Upgrade in Admin to unlock.
Lhdn.intermediaryConnected: Intermediary mode: {name} submits on behalf of each shop’s TIN via MyInvois.
Lhdn.intermediaryConnectedTuition: Intermediary mode: {name} submits on behalf of each tuition centre’s TIN via MyInvois.
Lhdn.demoMode: Demo mode: set LHDN_CLIENT_ID and LHDN_CLIENT_SECRET in env (platform intermediary credentials) to use real MyInvois.
